title: Euler's Formula on the Unit Circle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Euler's formula
unit circle
complex exponential
phasor
sine and cosine
electrical engineering
description: Interactive MicroSim showing the unit phasor e^(j*theta) on the complex plane. Its projection on the real axis is cos(theta) and its projection on the imaginary axis is sin(theta); two side plots trace both waveforms as the angle steps through key angles or rotates continuously.

educational.topic: Complex Numbers for AC Circuit Analysis
learningObjectives: Explain how Euler's formula relates rotating phasors to sinusoidal projections by observing the unit circle animation
prerequisites: complex numbers in rectangular and polar form
sine and cosine of standard angles

controls.label: Step
controls.description: Advance to the next key angle: 0, 30, 45, 60, 90, 180, 270, 360 degrees

controls.label: Back
controls.description: Return to the previous key angle

controls.label: Start / Stop
controls.description: Rotate the phasor continuously; starts stopped

controls.label: Waveforms
controls.description: Show or hide the cosine and sine plots

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict the projections at each key angle, then observe continuous rotation tracing the waveforms
keyQuestions: Which projection is the real part and which is the imaginary part?
Why does the cosine trace start at 1 while the sine trace starts at 0?
What does the picture show at 180 degrees, and how does that give Euler's identity?
commonMisconceptions: e raised to an imaginary power grows like an ordinary exponential
Sine is the horizontal projection and cosine is the vertical projection
assessmentOpportunities: Write e^(j*theta) in rectangular form for a given angle and sketch it on the unit circle
